### 4.161 The TLS trust chain aligns with the official batch: system roots on the data plane, the doctor's dual track (contract revision 1.163, 2026-10-15)

The empirical shape (2026-10-15, the user's real device): the user runs a
Shadowrocket proxy on macOS — TUN + fake-ip + the system HTTP proxy at
`127.0.0.1:1082`, its CA installed into the system keychain. On that machine
the official Signal desktop is **silently healthy** (Chromium rides the system
trust chain, and the user opted into the proxy's CA, so every MITM'd hop
validates), while our connector's data plane — the §4.38 step-3 CDN
attachment-download client — died on every download
(「对方发来的媒体暂时无法下载：附件数据不可用」). The root cause is one Cargo
feature: `rustls-tls-webpki-roots` bakes a compiled-in root set into the
binary, which never reads the system keychain and therefore can never trust
the CA the user themselves installed. The user's verdict, verbatim: 「别把
处理代理的任务给客户」 — handling the proxy is our job, not the customer's.
The alignment direction follows: **fix us, align with the official = trust
the system certificate store**; the user's proxy keeps zero changes and the
customer performs zero operations.

**① The data plane switches to the system trust chain.** The reqwest feature
swaps `rustls-tls-webpki-roots` → `rustls-tls-native-roots` — the rustls
stack kept, only the root *source* changes. `rustls-native-certs` 0.8.5 read
first-hand (the actual vendored source, not the docs): on macOS it walks the
Security.framework trust settings across `Domain::User → Admin → System`
(user overrides admin overrides system; an empty trust-settings array means
*always trust as root* — a user-installed CA in any domain lands in the
store); on Linux it reads the standard paths (honoring `SSL_CERT_FILE`/
`SSL_CERT_DIR`); on Windows the system store via `schannel`. The one client
this silently re-anchors is the `attachment_download_client` (supervisor) —
it configures no roots of its own, so it follows the feature; the doctor's
strict client pins its own anchor and is unaffected by the switch. No wire
face exists for a Cargo feature, so this move is recorded in-batch under this
revision without a schema touch. After this batch the connector's CDN
download accepts exactly the TLS reality the official desktop accepts — under
a MITM proxy the user trusted, and under no proxy at all, alike.

**② The doctor's dual-track adjudication (§4.79 wire face, additive).** The
strict probe pair (§4.79: chat + storage on the vendored Signal production
root CA, `tls_built_in_root_certs(false)` + `add_root_certificate` — the
kt-engine `tls_certs_only` attitude, the probe validating exactly the TLS
reality the engine's own traffic meets) keeps its name, its five
classification literals, and its bytes byte-for-byte. The batch adds a second
probe: the same chat target (`https://chat.signal.org/v1/accounts/whoami`),
the same launcher `socks5h://` route, the same 3-second budgets, redirects
off — on its own client built with **no custom anchor**, so it rides the
platform store (the feature switch above). The face key is
`service.systemTrust`, additive and optional, shaped exactly like its
siblings (`classification` always; `status`/`latencyMs` riding only with
`http`; the same fixed literal vocabulary — no sixth literal invented). The
presence rule: present exactly when `proxyConfigured` is true; on the
declared unconfigured face the key is **absent** — no probe ran, and absence
(not a `not_configured` literal) is how the wire says so; a system-trust
client build failure folds to `tls_failed` like the strict pair's build
failure always has. The two tracks are independent by construction (separate
clients, concurrent probes, either verdict stands alone). The consumption
contract: `chat`/`storage` classifying `tls_failed` while `systemTrust`
classifies `http` is the **official-equivalent usable** verdict — the
pinned-anchor plane fails but the system-trust plane works end to end, which
is precisely the user's MITM situation and precisely what the official
desktop tolerates silently. The desktop's proxy self-check
(`signalConnectivityCopy.ts` banner policy) is the downstream consumer batch;
this batch opens zero desktop tickets and only records the contract (see
boundaries).

**Site audit (the whole repository, all `reqwest::Client::builder()`
sites):** exactly four exist, three functional + one test fixture —
`doctor.rs service_client` (the strict leg, keeps its vendored pin,
deliberate), `doctor.rs system_trust_client` (new, the system-trust leg, no
anchor by design), `supervisor.rs attachment_download_client` (the data
plane, follows the feature → now system roots), and the `socks_refused`
doctor unit fixture (a dead loopback SOCKS proxy, fails before any TLS —
root source irrelevant). No `tls_built_in_root_certs(false)` /
`danger_accept_invalid_certs` counter-site exists anywhere else; the vendored
`vendor/certs/production-root-ca.pem` stays exactly where it is, still
consumed by the strict leg alone.

Boundaries, all recorded: **①the engine's `tls_certs_only` attitude is
untouched by this batch** — the kt-engine pins the same vendored Signal
production root CA as its single anchor for its own upstream traffic, and the
empirical evidence on the user's machine is that the engine's history-download
supplement worked fine under the same MITM environment (its pinned CA
validated the un-MITM'd Signal CDN chain), so there is no observed failure to
fix there; the strict doctor legs intentionally keep mirroring that engine
reality. **②the desktop consumer batch is downstream and unbilled here** —
the self-check banner policy (strict `tls_failed` + `systemTrust` `http` ⇒
pass, at most a non-blocking notice; only a `systemTrust` failure is a
genuinely broken link worth the blocking warning) is the contract recorded in
`docs/doctor-contract.md`; the desktop batch that consumes it lands
separately (queued behind this batch in the parity pipeline). **③the
no-system-certs environments are recorded honestly from the source** (reqwest
0.12.28 `async_impl/client.rs` read first-hand): an empty platform store with
zero load errors builds the client normally and every TLS handshake then
fails — the CDN downloads answer their existing UPSTREAM_ERROR face and the
doctor leg answers `tls_failed`; a store that yields zero valid and ≥1
invalid/error makes the client **build fail**, folding to the same
`tls_failed` literal (doctor) / `ServiceError::Io` (CDN client); ≥1 valid
root with parse failures keeps the valid ones (native stores often carry
ancient junk — reqwest's own precedent); there is **no webpki fallback** —
the compiled-in set is gone from the build, so a Linux container must ship
`ca-certificates` or all connector TLS fails honestly (this batch's CI runs
macOS and the full suite stays green; the boundary matters for future Linux
deployment).

Wire additive: one optional key on the §4.79 doctor report face, zero
existing keys moved or retyped, zero classification literals changed, zero
new methods/events/error codes/store moves/capability bits (the doctor rides
the handshake advertisement as always). Schema: no change — the schema
declares no `runtime.doctor` result def (the response's `result` is
free-form), so there is nothing to extend and the consistency pointers stay
put. Tests 853 → 855 (lib +2): the dual-track face forms
(`system_trust_face_rides_both_forms_additively` — the absent form keeping
the pre-1.163 key set exactly, the present form riding the sibling probe
shape next to untouched strict legs) and the independent client builds
(`dual_track_clients_build_independently` — the strict client keeps its
static vendored anchor, the system-trust client builds on the platform store
whatever it holds); the literal mapping is shared code already pinned by
`service_probe_classification_maps_every_literal` (its unconfigured arm now
also pins the key's absence), the structure test carries the present-form
assertions, and the integration `not_configured` test pins the absence over
the wire. The data plane has no feasible TLS unit test (a real CDN
handshake is not a fixture); recorded honestly — the full existing suite
(all local fake/mocked faces, HTTP loopback wiremock included) is the
regression, and the feature switch touches no test-visible byte of it.

### 4.162 The phone-number lookup relay: `phone.lookup` mirrors the engine's CDSI batch reader (contract revision 1.164, 2026-10-15)

The supply chain: the desktop D-batch (64584c27) lands find-by-phone-number
— a contact card's phone number resolving to an addressable recipient —
and its hostAdapter calls `supervisor.request("phone.lookup", {account,
numbers})` with the wire face locked first: the method name, the
`phone-lookup` capability tag, the Read lane, the batch cap, the `account`
param key (the value stays the opaque connector account id), and the
`{entries:[...]}` answer shape all arrive pre-pinned by that batch, and
this connector half registers the face without moving any of them. The
engine half is the `phoneLookup` CDSI batch reader (engine d088a59, its
compat §3 phone row and its §5 batch block): params
`{account, numbers[1..20]}` under the E.164 `^\+\d{7,15}$` shape gate, a
top-level JSON answer array in input order — each entry
`{number, aci?, pni?, isRegistered}` with single-hit semantics (a
ServiceId resolves as an Aci or a Pni, never both), null folding to
absence, and a miss arriving pre-degraded as
`{number, isRegistered: false}` — the usernameLookup discipline
(§4.55, §4.65) carried to phone numbers.

**① The connector side is registration, not invention.**
`prepare_phone_lookup` gates locally before any engine traffic — the
opaque account id validates, the batch answers its cap refusal
(`PHONE_LOOKUP_MAX_ENTRIES` = 20; the empty batch and the over-cap batch
both `INVALID_REQUEST`, retryable=false — the same refusals the desktop
hostAdapter gate answers), and every number passes the E.164 shape gate
(hand-written, the crate carries no regex dependency) — then the account
resolves to the engine's signal number and the frame leaves as
`{account: <signal number>, numbers}` verbatim. The engine's own
PHONE_INVALID stays the authority past the gate; the local gate answers
only the shapes the engine would refuse anyway, so the two gates never
disagree about a number the engine accepts.

**② The answer projects entry-for-entry from memory alone.** The
engine's top-level array becomes `{entries: [...]}` in input order, the
keys ride the engine's names verbatim, null folds to absence, no entry
is dropped or reordered. The projection is discard-after-render: nothing
lands in the connector store — the number→account local mapping stays
the contacts sync chain's (the §4.97 persist-nothing posture), and the
connector keeps no phone-number ledger of its own.

**③ The error faces ride the engine's literals through the global
structured-code mapping.** PHONE_INVALID deterministic (retryable=false,
no data — the message is the literal); PHONE_RATE_LIMITED carries the
promised `data.retryAfterSeconds` verbatim on the may-succeed-later
channel (retryable=true, the USERNAME_RATE_LIMITED channel: a later
attempt may succeed, the wait decision is the caller's, and nothing
retries automatically — the no-auto-retry red line covers a
rate-limit-shaped face the same as an unknown send outcome);
PHONE_SERVER_FAILED the same channel without data; the unknown-account
face stays the plain -32603 → UPSTREAM_ERROR ladder.

Wire additive: one new Read-lane method, one feature tag (`phone-lookup`
joining the constant feature table), three new error codes; zero new
events, zero store moves, zero capability bits. Schema: +2 defs
(phoneLookupParams / phoneLookupResult, the request branch pins the
result ref), the method enum +1, the error enum +3, the error `data`
description gains the retryAfterSeconds face; the consistency pairs +1
(numbers.maxItems ↔ PHONE_LOOKUP_MAX_ENTRIES), every pre-existing
pointer name-based and unmoved. Tests 855 → 860 (integration +3, lib
+2): the full-chain hit/miss relay
(`phone_lookup_rides_the_engine_projection_verbatim_hit_and_miss` — the
send log pinning the frame's `account` as the resolved signal number
with the numbers verbatim, the aci+pni hit and the pre-degraded miss
riding one answer, ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND on the unknown host account, zero
rows landing anywhere), the local gates refusing with zero engine
frames (`phone_lookup_local_gates_refuse_before_any_engine_traffic` —
the empty batch, the 21-number batch, four shape violations, the
boundary 20 passing), and the three error faces relayed honestly
(`phone_lookup_error_faces_ride_the_engine_literals_verbatim` — the
promised `retryAfterSeconds` 42 verbatim, no data invented on the
data-less faces, the rate-limit and server faces zero auto-retries);
the lib pair pins the preparation bounds/gates and the error faces'
retryability, the fake engine stub speaks the sentinel numbers, and the
handshake capabilities assertion carries the new method + tag.

### 4.163 The stop-the-bleeding batch: the pinned CDN root, the read-face issuance ledger, the decryption-error event, and the stall budgets (contract revision 1.165, 2026-10-16)

The empirical shape (2026-10-15/16, production): four independent wounds,
four minimal faces, every one a connector-local fix — the CDN attachment
download still dead on clean networks despite 1.163, the peer read
receipt re-sending the same batch on every trigger, the engine's
decryption-error report vanishing silently, and two unbounded waits (the
contacts sync that could hang forever, the link-time transfer wait that
gave up too early). None of them move a method, an error code, or a
capability bit; the wire grows one event, the store one column.

**① The CDN trust chain pins the vendored Signal production root.** The
1.163 native-roots client rejected every clean-network handshake exactly
like its webpki predecessor: the transit CDN's chain terminates at
Signal's own private root CA, carried by neither the webpki set nor any
platform keychain — two dead client generations for one missing anchor.
The fix is the anchor:
`vendor/certs/production-root-ca.pem` (the same pem the doctor's strict
probe pins) rides the download client via `add_root_certificate`,
compile-time (`include_bytes!`; a parse failure fails the client build).
reqwest 0.12.28's assembly order (read first-hand from the vendored
source): custom roots first, then webpki, then the native set — the
pinned anchor leads and the platform store stays loaded beneath it (the
`rustls-tls-native-roots` feature default), keeping 1.163's MITM-proxy
tolerance (a user-trusted proxy CA still validates, the official-desktop
Chromium-plus-system-store posture). The coarse
`tls_built_in_root_certs(false)` is deliberately NOT called — it would
drop the native leg too — and the webpki leg needs no off switch: the
`rustls-tls-webpki-roots` feature is not compiled into this dependency,
and the per-leg `tls_built_in_webpki_certs` toggle is 0.13 API that does
not exist on this build. Test: the vendored pem's SHA-256 pins the exact
bytes (a swapped or truncated file fails before any client rides it) plus
the parse-and-build pin; a real-CDN TLS handshake stays boundary-note
material (not unit-fixture material — the honest mount point is the
anchor's identity).

**② The peer read face grows an issuance ledger.** The wound:
`prepare_mark_read` had no completion step, and the §4.119 absent-mode
selection re-selected the whole seven-day window on every trigger — the
desktop's read-marker churn re-sent the same upstream timestamp batch
indefinitely (upstream-idempotent, so protocol-clean; the waste and churn
were ours). The fix mirrors the viewed face's §4.77 first-stamp
discipline: schema v25 adds the additive nullable
`messages.read_receipt_sent_at` (never backfilled — a past issuance is
only known from a fan-out that actually confirmed), and
`complete_mark_read` stamps the selection ONLY after the supervisor's
`sendReadReceipt` fan-out confirmed — a failed or unknown send must not
close the ledger, so the next deliberate trigger re-supplies the batch
(the §4.119 debounce holds the replay pressure in between). The stamp
covers the whole selection, including the group-conversation early
return: those rows' authors are unresolvable upstream (§4.28), nothing
will ever ride for them, so the ledger closes them out and stops the
reselection churn. The self-sync read face (`messages.syncRead`)
deliberately carries NO ledger: the desktop fires `messages.markRead`
(the readReceipts-flag-gated peer face) and `messages.syncRead` (the
unconditional self-sync) as independent channels, and a shared ledger
would let one channel's confirmed send silence the other — the sync
channel's replays are self-addressed and protocol-idempotent.
`ReceiptResupply` types the per-face boundary: `UnissuedRead` (peer read,
`read_receipt_sent_at IS NULL`), `UnplayedViewed` (both viewed faces,
§4.77), `Any` (self-sync read). The ledger is connector bookkeeping
only — `read_at` stays the §4.81 cross-device sync's projection, and the
explicit-`messageIds` mode applies no boundary (the desktop naming ids is
itself the incremental act).

**③ The decryption-error envelope gains a consumption arm.** The engine
already reports inbound envelopes it cannot decrypt — as a `receive`
notification whose envelope carries the `decryptionError` marker
(`{account, envelope: {sourceUuid, decryptionError: {}, timestamp?}}`,
the engine's structured report) — and the connector silently dropped it
at the receive arm: no metric, no event, no trace. The fix routes it
before the receive ladder (a marker envelope never carries a message
row; there is nothing to project): the parse diverts to the
account-domain event lane with the accountUnbound attribution
discipline (a missing, empty, or non-string account falls back to the
unknownNotification warning — never an invented identity), producing
`EngineEvent::ReceiveDecryptionError`; the registry files it with the
watcher-owned events; the watcher arm counts it into the metrics
snapshot (`decryption_errors_total`) and forwards
`HostSideEvent::ReceiveDecryptionError` → the wire frame
`receive.decryptionError {accountId}`. Pure observability: nothing
persists, and NO reset action exists on this face — decryption failures
self-heal through the engine's own DERM retry protocol, and an automatic
session reset here would be the self-inflicted reset storm the official
client explicitly avoids. An unmatchable account drops warn-only (the
lane's discipline), the perf counter makes the drop visible, and the
metrics snapshot counts independently of the event stream — a missed
frame costs nothing.

**④ The two stall budgets.** `contacts.sync` had no budget: a stalled
leg (a starved service lock, a store stall, a wedged engine call) hung
the desktop's sync empty state forever. The engine-and-store pass now
rides one 120 s wall-clock budget (`CONTACTS_SYNC_BUDGET`; the 60 s
cache short-circuit stays outside it), folding to the retryable
`UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT` face (the link-finish timeout's precedent) — the
caller re-triggers when it chooses, nothing retries automatically. And
the link-time history-transfer wait widens 10 min → 60 min
(`LINK_WAIT_MS`): a real archive transfer over a slow proxy outlives the
old ceiling, and the importer was declaring defeat mid-transfer (the
engine side widens its own budget to match, in parallel).

Wire additive: one event enum entry (`receive.decryptionError`) + one
allOf branch pinning `{accountId}`; store schema v24 → v25 (additive
nullable column, no backfill); zero new methods, error codes, or
capability bits. Schema consistency holds by the standing discipline
(the frame literal and the enum entry move together — the consistency
test pins both directions). Tests 860 → 865 (lib +5): the CDN anchor pin
(`download_client_pins_the_vendored_signal_root` — the SHA-256 identity
plus the parse-and-build), the ledger once-only discipline
(`mark_read_ledger_supplies_each_row_once` — a confirmed fan-out closes
the selection, a failed one re-supplies byte-identically, the sync face
ignores the ledger, `read_at`/`viewed_at` stay untouched), the schema
step (`schema_v25_upgrade_adds_read_receipt_sent_at` — the ladder
landing, history rows NULL, the version stamp moving), the envelope
diversion (`receive_decryption_error_envelope_routes_to_the_event_lane`
— one attributed event and an empty queue, the unattributed trio, the
marker-free envelope still queueing), and the transfer-wait pin
(`link_wait_window_covers_the_engine_transfer_budget`); the lane test
and the wire-frame test gain the fifth arm
(`account_transient_lane_resolves_or_drops_unattributed`,
`engine_notification_events_ride_their_contract_frames`), and the
metrics snapshot test carries the new series key.

### 4.164 The wait window watches the transfer: `history.importStatus` pending carries the live download face (contract revision 1.166, 2026-10-16)

The wound (2026-10-15, transfer-observation audit): during the link-time wait
window the desktop polled `history.importStatus` and got the bare
`{accountId, state: "pending"}` — static "preparing" copy for the entire
up-to-60-min window — while the engine's transfer snapshot was live the whole
time. The engine's window has two stretches: the `transfer_archive` long poll
waiting for the phone to produce and upload the archive (most of the window,
snapshot at `bytesRead: 0`, no total — no numbers exist yet), then the CDN
streaming stretch (bytes accumulating, a total once a content-length is
read). The connector consulted that snapshot in pending since §4.146 — but
only to consume a terminal: a live snapshot with no `errorCode` changed
nothing, so the honest answer stayed the bare pending face and the desktop
had nothing to render until the connector's own import row went `running`,
which happens only after the archive has fully landed. The running face's
§4.51 progress contract was exactly the missing half.

**The fix is a second consumer on the same single consult, failure priority
unchanged.** The wait-window `pending` still reads `transfer.downloadStatus`
once per poll (the consult-flag discipline untouched — a disk-pending, the
archive-present face, still never consults: no stale terminal may land a
failed row beside an archive the connector is about to import, and none may
decorate it with stale progress either). A snapshot carrying a consumable
`errorCode` resolves exactly as §4.146 taught: `no_archive` onto the
information class, every other code onto an immediate persisted failed row.
A snapshot without one is the live transfer, and it now rides the same
§4.51 shape gate (`import_progress_from_engine_snapshot`) the running face
uses: `progress: {stage: "downloading", bytesTransferred?, bytesTotal?}` on
the pending answer — byte brothers together only when the engine read a
content-length, stage alone otherwise (the long-poll stretch answers
`bytesRead: 0` with no total, and the gate renders that as stage alone,
never a zero-filled guess). Absent snapshot (engine down, restarted,
success-cleared), malformed byte shape, or transferred > total: the
pre-1.166 bare pending, byte for byte — no progress invented. The
`processing` stage is deliberately unreachable on pending: it names the
connector's own NDJSON import pass, which by definition holds a `running`
row, not a pending face.

**The failure-code face stays a verbatim pass-through — re-pinned, not
changed.** `engine_import_failure_code` is a shape gate (non-empty string
within [`MAX_IMPORT_FAILURE_CODE_CHARS`]), never a whitelist: the code rides
the failed row's `errorClass` exactly as the engine spelled it, and the
engine is the word list's owner. The engine's new terminal vocabulary —
`relink_requested` and `continue_without_upload`, same wire face as the
existing `no_archive`/`network`/`cdn_unreachable`/`decode_failed`/`io` —
therefore needs zero connector change: both codes land immediate persisted
failed rows with `errorClass` verbatim, one attempt, exactly like every code
before them. The connector adds no semantics and no translation (only
`no_archive` is special-cased, the §4.146 information class); the desktop
decides the copy per code.

Wire additive: one optional `progress` key on one state face; zero new
methods, events, error codes, capability bits, or store moves. Schema
consistency holds unchanged (the result stays free-form; the contract text
lives in the `historyImportStatusParams` description). Tests: the
wait-window pending projection pair
(`wait_window_pending_projects_live_download_progress` — byte brothers,
stage-only during the long-poll stretch, bare pending without a snapshot,
and the disk-pending never-consults boundary) and the verbatim-code pin
(`engine_relink_and_continue_without_upload_codes_land_failed_rows_verbatim`
— the two new engine codes land `errorClass` verbatim, one attempt each,
persisted); the lib gate test carries the new vocabulary
(`engine_import_failure_code_gate`), and the §4.146 tests stand unchanged —
the failure consumption keeps priority over the progress face.

### 4.165 The `engine call failed` log carries the engine's cause class (contract revision 1.167, 2026-10-16)

The wound (2026-10-16, intermittent-send audit): the engine folds a
send-chain transport failure into the plain internal_error face (-32603)
whose `message` embeds the cause class (§4.80), and the connector
classifies only the four frozen anchor literals — rate limit, proof
challenge, server unavailability, the identity gate. A cause outside that
set degraded to the generic upstream family, and the raw error body — the
only place the cause was ever visible — was dropped at the response
classifier, so the `engine call failed` log line named the failure
`error_class="upstream"` with nothing underneath: an intermittent send
could not be attributed to a transport family from the field.

**The fix surfaces the embedded literal; it does not widen the
classifier.** The frozen §4.80/§4.95 anchor set is a wire contract and
stays byte-frozen. The generic upstream arm now runs `upstream_error_cause`
over the same message and carries the tailmost parenthesized class-name
literal on the error itself (`EngineError::Upstream { cause }`), bounded
to 120 bytes (`ENGINE_ERROR_CAUSE_MAX_BYTES`; oversize truncates). The log
line gains one field on that face only: `cause="(SomeException)"` after
`error_class` — a fixed engine class literal, never free-form text. The
shape gate is the content red line: a candidate token must be letter-led
and `[A-Za-z0-9._]`-only (the §4.80 anchor family's shape), so message
text, phone numbers, contact names, digit-led timestamps, and any
whitespace-bearing prose cannot ride the field; the tailmost position is
the contract-pinned one (the cause class embedded at the message tail), so
an earlier incidental token never wins.

Zero wire change: the host answer stays `UPSTREAM_ERROR` byte for byte
(the cause never reaches an `ApiError`), the auto-retry schedule keeps
mapping the upstream family to Backoff regardless of the cause, and no
schema, method, event, or error-code face moves. Everything but the
cause-bearing face keeps the pre-1.167 line byte for byte: the other
error classes carry no message at all, an upstream message with no
class-shaped token answers `None` and emits the old line, and the
emit-site's no-cause arm is the unchanged source line.

Tests (lib +4): the extraction unit
(`upstream_error_cause_extracts_the_tail_class_literal_bounded` — the
tailmost token wins over an earlier incidental one, the dotted FQN
literal, the shape-hostile ladder: no parens, space-bearing prose, a
`+`-led phone token, a digit-led token, an unclosed paren, an empty
wrapper, missing and non-string messages, and the 120-byte truncation),
the log-face pair (`engine_call_failed_log_carries_the_upstream_cause` /
`engine_call_failed_log_stays_byte_identical_outside_the_cause` — the
cause line's field set with the bound riding whole at the emitter, and
the regression pin that a non-upstream class and a causeless upstream
emit no `cause=`), and the through-the-wire carry
(`generic_upstream_error_carries_the_embedded_cause_literal` — the
response handler attaches the extracted literal, a shape-hostile message
stays causeless, neither emits an account event). The existing
generic-upstream fixtures update to the carried literal
(`(UserErrorException)`) and to the causeless shape.

### 4.166 The boot-window send-integrity audit: the three send questions closed honest, the stalled-dispatch log line (no-revision record, 2026-10-16)

The wound (2026-10-16, the intermittent-send window): during one boot
window the desktop sidebar showed send checkmarks the connector had no
row for, three host requests stayed pending forever, and a text the
user typed never surfaced in the connector at all. The audit asked three
questions before touching anything: which code paths can answer a send
ok with no engine round trip; how an Unbound-window text failure
settles; and whether the engine's request/response matching could let a
typing ok complete a text's row.

All three close honest — nothing in the audited behavior is wrong.

**(a) The engine-free send faces are bounded and none flips state.** Four
families answer a send-shaped request without an engine round trip: the
receipt funnel's empty-group short-circuit (`Ok("sent")` when no group
needs a receipt) and its failure-debounce answer (`Ok("unknown")` inside
the cooldown); the pure-local send-lane writes (draft save/clear, the
local contact alias — the engine stays out of the path by design); and
the clientRequestId idempotent answer, which returns the already-stored
row unchanged. None of these invents a delivery: the receipt faces move
no message row, the local writes touch no message row, and the
idempotent answer is the honest projection of a row that already exists
— the desktop reconnect-resend contract face, deliberately left
untouched. The sidebar's checkmarks in this window were never connector
attestation: that text has no row, no engine dispatch trace, and no
host completion on the connector side.

**(b) The Unbound-window failure settlement is armed, and this window's
text never entered the funnel.** A send inserts its pending row under
the deterministic (account, conversation, clientRequestId) identity
before the engine call; an upstream-family engine error settles the row
failed and arms the automatic Backoff schedule atomically, and the host
answer carries `UPSTREAM_ERROR` with `retryable=true`; an unknown face
retires the row as unknown and nothing retries it. That machinery was
simply not reached: this window's text left no row, no engine dispatch
trace, and no host completion (the send metrics closed as ok+rejected
only, with the unknown face at zero and the pending requests never
answered). The desktop's "send outcome pending" fold came from the
desktop side — its own request timeout and mutating-call
disconnect-folding answer `unknown_outcome` locally when the connector
stops answering within the desktop's own budget; the connector's
unknown-face completion path requires an engine answer, and the engine
never saw the send. The scattered `engine call failed` lines in the
same window were the outbox retrying old failed rows on the capped
backoff rhythm, not this text.

**(c) Cross-request resolution is impossible.** Engine request ids are
monotonic per connection; a response resolves strictly by removing its
own id from the pending map, and an id with no waiting request is a
protocol warning and nothing else — it cannot complete any call. A
oneshot resolves only the request it was paired with. Typing has no
pending row to settle by construction, and a send's row settlement is
bound to the engine call inside the same dispatch arm, with the row
matched on the full (message id, account, conversation) key. A typing
ok therefore cannot complete a text's pending row, and in this window
the text's row did not exist anywhere in the connector to complete.

**The audit's real finding is the blind spot, and the repair is one
log line.** An admitted-but-never-completed host dispatch — exactly the
three forever-pending requests and the swallowed send above — currently
ends with no trace once the process restarts. A dispatch still in
flight after every bounded budget has run out (engine calls are
timeout-capped at seconds, media downloads at two minutes) now warns
once per request, carrying the method name, its class, the account, the
request byte size, and the stall threshold; `link.*` waits are exempt
because their approval window is legitimately long. The line answers
nothing on the wire, changes no state, adds no method, event, error
code, capability, store face, or metric — it exists so the next
intermittent-send window names its stalled requests instead of
replaying this audit.

Tests (lib +1, integration +3): the strict-resolution pin
(`response_for_another_request_cannot_resolve_the_waiting_call` — a
response for one pending request resolves only that request, a second
request stays waiting, and an unknown id warns and resolves nothing),
and the three integration pins against the fake engine — the generic
upstream failure settles the row failed, arms the Backoff schedule,
answers `UPSTREAM_ERROR` retryable, and the automatic retry then settles
it sent with exactly two upstream calls
(`generic_upstream_failure_settles_failed_arms_the_schedule_and_answers_retryable`);
a duplicate clientRequestId re-answers the stored row with no second
engine call (`duplicate_send_text_answers_the_persisted_row_without_engine_traffic`);
and a typing success writes no row and touches no send face beyond its
own upstream call (`typing_success_writes_no_row_and_touches_no_send_face`).

### 4.167 The group-history resync: opening the conversation becomes the group-refresh trigger (no-revision record, 2026-10-16)

The wound (2026-10-16, the "gggg" group): the desktop opened a group
conversation to an empty message window and a "0 members" header, while
the sidebar preview carried the account's own "你: 1 01:15 ✓" row. The
forensics, all read-only:

**(a) The message window emptiness is not a connector rejection and not a
missing import.** The desktop's timeline read is `messages.list`, and its
connector ladder gates on exactly two rows — the account row and the
conversation row (`store_list_messages`) — never on group state, so a
`GROUP_NOT_FOUND` cannot reject it. The group's message row exists in the
connector store: the sidebar preview's direction and send-state faces are
read-time projections of the newest `messages` row
(`conversation_last_message_meta`), and "你: … ✓" is only reachable when
that row is there. The desktop-side rendering gate is its own: the roster
read that failed during the boot window leaves the group details null and
the member subtitle falls back to the roster length (zero), and the
timeline load early-returns while the runtime transition gate holds —
neither is a connector answer. The connector side of the wound is the
cache miss below.

**(b) The "0 members" face is the desktop's fallback over a connector
cache miss.** The conversation summary carries no member count at all;
the connector's only member-count face is `groups.get`, projected from
the contacts row's `extra` JSON (`memberCount`/`members`, written only by
a contacts pull). With the contacts row missing, `groups.get` answers the
existing `GROUP_NOT_FOUND` cache arm (`retryable=false`) and the desktop
renders zero from its own fallback. The row was missing because the boot
window's only automatic pull had already failed: the startup re-sync runs
once, two seconds after the engine lands, and the engine needed ~13.5s to
bind — the field log shows the exact shape (two instant `listGroups`
upstream failures and the `GROUP_NOT_FOUND` host rejection in the same
millisecond window), and nothing ever retried. The three manual
`contacts.sync` triggers were never fired.

**The repair aligns the official lazy group update.** The official
desktop refreshes a group on conversation open under a five-minute TTL
(`waitThenMaybeUpdateGroup`, `FIVE_MINUTES`), clears the timestamp on a
failed update so the next open retries immediately
(`setLastSuccessfulGroupFetch(id, undefined)`), and folds a
nonexistent-group answer into left semantics (`GROUP_NONEXISTENT` →
`generateLeftGroupChanges`). The connector mirror:

- A `groups.get` whose cached read misses (`GROUP_NOT_FOUND`) or whose
  roster is empty (no `memberCount`, or zero — never a terminated row)
  triggers ONE single-group engine `listGroups` refresh under the same
  5-minute TTL, in-memory and bounded (a fixed entry cap: past the cap a
  new stamp is refused, so that one group keeps reaching the engine —
  never an unbounded map). A successful refresh backfills the row through the
  passive upsert — the same columns and conflict semantics as the sync
  persist, deliberately NOT advancing the account-wide
  `contacts_synced_at` marker — and replays the original read, with the
  live requesting/pending faces projected from the same engine answer.
  The throttle stamps success only: a failed refresh (engine not bound
  yet, engine refused, store write failed) clears the stamp so the next
  open retries immediately, which is also what makes the boot window
  self-heal — the incident's exact shape (read at T+2s, engine bound at
  T+13.5s) converges on the next conversation open without any manual
  `contacts.sync`.
- A definitive negative — the engine answered the single-group listing
  and the group is absent from it, or present with `isMember != true` —
  writes the existing §4.50 appendix terminated face onto the group's
  cache row (only when the conversation already exists; a garbage key
  materializes nothing) and replays the read carrying `isTerminated`:
  the connector has no left bit, so the terminated face is the recorded
  stand-in, and a terminated row never re-pulls. An engine that is not
  ready or refuses the read is NOT a negative: the answer stays the
  pre-existing `GROUP_NOT_FOUND` face byte for byte.
- The message rows need no replay leg: they were never missing (a), and
  the read ladder has no group gate to reject them.

Zero wire change: no new method, event, error code, capability, schema
move, or metric; every answer (including the degrade) keeps its
pre-1.167 shape, `conversation.changed` rides only through the §4.135
semantics the pull and the passive batch already share, and the error
faces the desktop already consumes are untouched. The engine's own group
gate stays the authority past the trigger: the connector still never
decodes a group id (the §4.150 opaque-transit posture), and the
connector-side roster write is the same projection the sync persist has
run since §4.39.

Tests (integration +4, all against the fake engine): the cache miss
resyncs, backfills, and replays the read
(`group_cache_miss_resyncs_replays_and_backfills_the_roster`); the
throttle holds within the TTL — the backfilled row removed, the next
read answers the cache-miss face again without a second refresh
(`group_resync_throttles_within_the_ttl_after_success`); a definitive
negative marks the terminated face and stops re-pulling — the fixture's
former-group entry (`isMember=false`) and, under the empty-listing
marker, an absent id both land on the same arm, the row persists
`isTerminated`, and the next read answers the terminated face without a
refresh
(`group_true_negative_marks_terminated_and_stops_repulling`); and the
boot-window shape self-heals — a read with no engine answers the
untouched `GROUP_NOT_FOUND` face, and after the engine lands the same
read succeeds with no manual sync
(`group_boot_window_degrades_then_self_heals_once_the_engine_lands`).

### 4.168 The bounded host dispatch answer: every admitted request answers within the stall budget (contract revision 1.168, 2026-10-16)

The wound (the Main↔connector RPC queue batch forensics): the desktop
showed read requests timing out at its own 30s face while the connector
logged zero completed requests, and an earlier window had left
`host_pending_requests=3` stuck permanently. The forensic chain, all
read-only:

**(a) The desktop queue is not where the request stopped being honest, but
it is where the user felt it.** The desktop Main scheduler
(`requestScheduler.ts`) bounds four lanes (control 1, linkWait 1, read 4,
send 2) with per-queue soft timeouts; a queued task evicted after 10s
answers `queue_timeout` — the literal "请求排队超时，请求未发出" banner.
The connector client (`connectorClient.ts`) times each request out at 30s
and folds a non-mutating timeout into a plain error, which the host
payload path turns into `internal_error` (`retryable=false`) — a terminal
face on what is a transient transport condition. Both faces are honest
about "never reached the wire work", but neither is the root cause.

**(b) The connector could strand an admitted request forever.** Three
never-answer shapes existed past every budgeted face:

1. **Lane-permit starvation.** A dispatch's lane wait (`acquire`) has no
   timeout. Control holds exactly one permit, so a single wedged control
   dispatch parked every later control request in the semaphore forever —
   admitted into the pending budget (the gauge counts them), never
   dispatched, never answered, never warned: the §4.166 stall warn arms
   only after the permit is granted.
2. **The wedged dispatch itself.** The §4.166 warn fires at 300s and then
   deliberately answers nothing: a dispatch stuck past every face budget
   (engine calls are seconds-capped, CDN two minutes — the budget that
   escaped is a non-engine face such as a store lock or a blocked write)
   held its lane permit, its pending-budget slot and the answer itself
   forever.
3. **The stale gauge.** The connection teardown drains in-flight
   dispatches for 5s and then gives up; a wedged dispatch leaves the
   process-global `host_pending_requests` at a count nothing will ever
   decrement — the "3 forever" shape.

The engine call path was never the hole: `call_with_timeout` bounds every
engine request (timeout → `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`/`SEND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, a
dropped oneshot → `UPSTREAM_EXITED`, a dead engine → `NotRunning`), so
bootstrap, engine restart handover and engine death all answer inside
their budgets already.

**The repair bounds every admitted dispatch to the §4.166 budget.** Both
the lane-permit wait and the dispatch execution are wrapped in the same
`HOST_DISPATCH_STALL_WARN_AFTER` deadline (300s — beyond the CDN face,
the longest real budget):

- expiry on the permit wait warns once with the §4.166 field set (an
  acquire-shaped message) and answers the retryable `INTERNAL_ERROR`
  deadline face — the request provably never started, so the face is
  honest for every method class;
- expiry on the dispatch emits the §4.166 warn byte for byte and answers
  the same retryable `INTERNAL_ERROR` face carrying the original request
  id; the abandoned future drops at its await point, releasing every guard
  it holds (lane permit, account mutex, store locks) exactly like a
  connection teardown already does;
- `link.*` stays exempt from both (the §4.166 exemption: approval windows
  are legitimately long);
- the connection exit resets `host_pending_requests` to zero after the
  drain, so a finished session can no longer leave the gauge stuck.

Zero wire vocabulary change: no new method, event, error code, capability,
or schema move — the deadline face reuses the `INTERNAL_ERROR` retryable
shape the capacity face already teaches the desktop. The answerability
contract changes, which is what the 1.168 revision records. The stall warn
is preserved (now terminal on the dispatch arm), and the §4.166 log-only
behaviour survives verbatim on the `link.*` exemption.

Tests (+4 lib): the starved permit answers the deadline face within the
budget and leaves the lane free
(`starved_lane_permit_answers_the_deadline_face_within_the_stall_budget`);
a wedged dispatch answers the deadline face carrying the original request
id (`wedged_dispatch_answers_the_deadline_face_within_the_stall_budget`);
the `link.*` exemption stays unbounded
(`link_waits_stay_exempt_from_the_stall_budget`); and a full session ends
with the pending gauge at zero
(`connection_exit_resets_the_host_pending_gauge`).

### 4.169 The bounded host answer write-back: a wedged peer parks a writer task, never the session loop (contract revision 1.169, 2026-10-16)

The wound (the 2026-10-16 03:48–04:22Z read-lane wedge, the session after
the user's 12:04 restart): the connector (pid 21694, engine 21695, the
e74a8f5 build — sources last touched 03:28:35Z, the release binary built
03:37:50Z, both before the 03:48Z session start, and the dev resolver
prefers `KT_SIGNAL_CONNECTOR_BIN` pointing at that release binary) served
its boot burst normally — 125 read and 28 send completions, the last one
logged at 04:05:58.304Z — and then froze completely: every metrics
snapshot from 04:06:50Z to the log's end at 04:21:50Z repeats
`host_pending_requests=4` with zero further request completions. That is
15+ minutes stuck, three times the §4.168 answer deadline, with the
process demonstrably alive (the metrics task kept ticking every 60s) and
**zero** §4.166/§4.168 stall warns: the deadlines were armed but never
observed. The engine log shows the same silence from its side — after the
03:53:35Z `listGroups` answers (pre-restart) and the 04:05:58Z one
(post-restart), no engine call arrives at all while the Signal websocket
keepalive diagnostics keep streaming — so the wedge is connector-side,
downstream of every engine budget.

The gap §4.168 left open, in code: the deadline wrapper
(`dispatch_within_stall_budget`) bounds only the dispatch execution. The
answer write that follows it — `send_shared(&task_writer, &response).await`
— is an unbounded await on the host socket's writability, and the session
loop's own writes (reject answers, registry events, host events) are
unbounded awaits too. A host that stops reading its Unix socket fills the
kernel buffer and every subsequent write parks forever. Two wedge shapes
follow, both past every deadline:

1. **The parked response write-back.** A dispatch whose execution
   completed logs its answer line and then parks inside its own
   `send_shared`: the `DispatchCompletion` never returns, the
   pending-budget slot never releases, and no deadline covers the await —
   the §4.168 wrapper already passed. The last logged completion
   (04:05:58.304Z, `send ok duration_ms=0`) is exactly this shape: an
   answer computed, logged, and never provably delivered.
2. **The frozen session loop.** One parked write inside any `select!` arm
   (an event forward, a reject) stops the loop from ever re-entering the
   poll — and `FuturesUnordered`'s futures only advance when the loop
   polls them. Every in-flight dispatch freezes mid-await; its deadline
   timer fires, wakes the future, and the wake queues behind a poll that
   never comes. This is the shape that explains zero stall warns on a
   live process: an armed `tokio` timer cannot fire through a task that
   is parked inside a single unbounded await.

Which of the two parked first in the 04:05:58Z wedge is not
distinguishable from the surviving logs (the pre-restart connector log
was truncated by the restart; the post-restart log holds both shapes'
joint signature — frozen completions, stuck gauge, silent deadlines).
Both share one root cause and both are repaired together.

**The repair mirrors the engine's A7 stdin-writer discipline.** All
post-authentication host writes — dispatch responses, reject answers,
registry events, host events — enqueue a pre-serialized frame into a
bounded per-session queue (`HOST_WRITE_QUEUE_CAPACITY`, 256 frames,
count-bounded) drained by a single writer task that owns the sink: one
writer, one order. Enqueue never awaits writability:

- a saturated queue drops the frame with a log-only warn; on the
  response arm the pending budget still releases (the dispatch future
  always completes, `host_pending_requests` stays truthful), on the
  event arm the event is dropped (the same lossy shape as the existing
  broadcast-backpressure `eventBackpressure` face, which predates this
  batch). A peer that stopped reading wedges only the writer task;
- the writer task's own I/O failure (peer gone mid-frame) forwards
  through a bounded failure channel into the `select!` loop as a new arm
  and ends the session exactly as a direct write error did — the
  `PeerGone` normalization and the teardown path are unchanged;
- the loop itself never parks on a host write, so every §4.168 deadline
  stays observable and the answerability claim becomes structural:
  admit → acquire ≤300s → dispatch ≤300s → enqueue (non-blocking) →
  delivery best-effort by the writer task. The pre-authentication
  challenge/handshake writes keep their direct framed form (bounded by
  `HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` on the read side, single small frames before any
  wedge surface exists).

Zero wire change: the frames, their order (one queue, one consumer), and
every face are byte-identical; a healthy peer observes no difference in
latency (enqueue is a bounded-channel push the writer drains
immediately). The new `HostError::WriteBackSaturated` is internal-only
(never reaches the host or the exit status), matching the `PeerGone`
discipline. The §4.166/§4.168 stall warns keep their bytes; the new
saturation warns are separate log-only faces carrying
`method`/`method_class`/`account_id`/`request_bytes` (response arm) or
the event kind (event arm).

Tests (+3 lib): a non-reading peer wedges only the writer — a follow-up
request still completes and releases its budget slot
(`wedged_peer_parks_the_writer_task_and_the_session_loop_stays_alive`);
a saturated queue drops the response with the warn face and the truthful
gauge (`saturated_write_queue_drops_the_answer_warns_and_releases_the_budget`);
a writer I/O failure still ends the session like a direct write error
(`writer_io_failure_still_ends_the_session`).

### 4.170 The canonical memo key: the self conversation lives on the account's ACI (contract revision 1.170, 2026-10-16)

The Note-to-Self conversation is the one conversation whose peer is the
linked account itself, and its store key has been ambiguous since the ACI
became queryable. Contract 1.43 (§4.42) keyed the self chat by the account's
own number and recorded the boundary honestly: "the own ACI is not
queryable on either engine's jsonRpc surface, so a UUID-shaped peer key
cannot be marked." Contract 1.142 (§4.138) then made the ACI queryable and
persisted it on the account row. Three writers kept keying the self chat by
number — the contacts-sync materialization, the ingest of an own-number
envelope, the history import of the self chat — while the receive path's
self-mirror carries `sourceUuid` = the own ACI, so the two key families
describe the same conversation and a store can hold both: a number-keyed
shell (sent history, contacts material) beside an ACI-keyed row (received
mirror). The desktop shows two self chats; the unread counts split.

**The canonical key is the ACI** (`accounts.aci`): it is the Signal-native
identity the receive path already speaks, it survives number churn, and the
send path resolves it directly (the engine's `resolve_recipient` parses a
UUID service id on its first ladder arm — verified read-only). The
number-keyed row is a shell to fold, never a second conversation.

**The redirect (write-time unification).** `Store::ensure_conversation`
checks one predicate before its existing body: `kind == "direct"` and
`peer_key` equals the account's own `signal_account` and the account
carries an `aci` distinct from that number → the call re-keys to
`(direct, aci)` (title rides). The redirected call cannot loop: its peer
key is the ACI, which fails the equals-the-number test; the degenerate
`aci == signal_account` answer redirects nothing. Every path that
materializes or touches the self chat through `ensure_conversation` —
contacts sync, ingest, history import — lands canonical from then on. The
§6.5 contacts-sync and §4.122 passive-batch skeleton materializers do not
route through `ensure_conversation` — their insert loops apply the same
predicate directly (`skeleton_conversation_peer_key`), so the own entry
lands canonical there too while their contacts-cache rows keep the number
key (the §4.43 contacts face is untouched). The `memo_migrations` ledger
row dies with its account (the FK cascades): a fold ledger must never
outlive the account it folded, or `accounts.deleteLocalData` fails its FK.
Read paths that query a conversation by an explicit id or by a non-self
peer key are untouched.

**The predicates (read-time truth).** `peer_key_is_self` now matches the
stored ACI beside the number, and the §4.42/§4.43 summary and contacts
derivations pass the account row's `aci` through — one column in the same
single-row account lookup they already hold. A canonical `(direct, aci)`
row is `isSelf: true`; a stranger's UUID-keyed row still never is. The
§4.24 recorded boundary ("the own ACI cannot be marked") is superseded by
1.142's answer, and this paragraph records the supersession.

**The backfill (store-level fold).** `Store::normalize_memo_identity(
account_id) -> Option<ConversationSummary>` runs inside one transaction:

1. Read the account row; no ACI, or an ACI equal to the number → `None`
   (nothing to fold, and the redirect would be a no-op anyway).
2. The canonical row is ensured at `(direct, aci)` (title: the shell's
   current title when a shell exists, else the account's display name or
   number). No shell row → `None`: a store with only canonical state is
   already done; the canonical row is not pre-created for accounts that
   never materialized a self chat (the redirect creates it on first real
   touch, so the conversation list never grows empty placeholders).
3. Messages move with an `UPDATE … SET conversation_id = canonical WHERE
   conversation_id = shell AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM messages other
   WHERE other.conversation_id = canonical AND other.account_id =
   messages.account_id AND other.direction = messages.direction AND
   other.sent_at = messages.sent_at AND other.sender_id =
   messages.sender_id)` — the signal-identity tuple the
   `messages_signal_identity_v2` index already sorts. The table carries NO
   unique constraint on that tuple, so the dedupe is this guard, not a
   constraint; rows that would duplicate stay shell-side and are deleted
   (the canonical copy wins — it is the row the desktop reads). A deleted
   duplicate takes its `message_edits` history with it (the edits FK
   cascades); edits on the kept copy are untouched. Message ids do not
   change on the moved rows, so every id-keyed side reference stays valid.
4. `message_events` (reactions, keyed by conversation + target timestamp)
   move under the same `NOT EXISTS` guard on their own unique tuple
   `(account_id, conversation_id, kind, target_timestamp, actor_id)`;
   duplicates drop. The table's conversation FK has no cascade, so this
   step is what keeps the shell row deletable.
5. `conversation_pins` / `conversation_drafts` rows move when the
   canonical row lacks one (PK `(account_id, conversation_id)`); the
   shell's rows cascade away with the shell.
6. Conversation state merges shell → canonical: `title` through
   `title_should_upgrade` (a real name upgrades, a mask never); `unread_
   count` and `unread_mentions` take the MAX; `muted` and `pinned` OR;
   `expire_timer_seconds`, `mrr_factors_json`, `last_message_at` and
   `last_message_preview` keep the canonical's own stamp when present and
   take the shell's otherwise (recency resolves the preview pair).
7. The shell row is deleted. A `memo_migrations` ledger row is written:
   `account_id` (PK), `canonical_aci`, `source_peer_key`, `rollback_json`
   (the shell row verbatim plus the ids of dropped duplicates),
   `migrated_at`. The answer is the refreshed canonical summary (its
   `isSelf` now true).

The fold is idempotent: a second call finds no shell and answers `None`.
The schema moves 25 → 26 for the `memo_migrations` table alone (created by
the schema string, so old databases gain it on open; no backfill at open
time — the fold runs at the seams, where the ACI is fresh and the
announcement channel exists).

**The seams.** The migration runs exactly where the ACI is (re)written
with a host-facing lane to announce on: after the account sync persists
each engine-reported ACI, and after `link.finish` persists the finish
answer. Both seams fold the account's shell and, when a fold happened,
send `HostSideEvent::ConversationChanged` with the canonical summary —
the desktop's open list re-reads one row instead of two.

**The recorded boundary: the old-ACI era is not migrated.** The reference
store holds 18 rows keyed by a stale own-ACI from a previous link era
(peer keys like `c9bf3cad-…`). No safe predicate distinguishes a stale
own-ACI row from a stranger's ACI-keyed conversation — an ACI the account
once answered with is indistinguishable, at fold time, from an ACI another
human owns. A wrong merge silently moves one person's history into
another's conversation: a data incident, not a migration. Those rows stay
exactly as they are; only the row keyed by the CURRENT `accounts.aci` is
canonical, and the current ACI is what both the redirect and the fold key
on. Rollback, if ever needed, is an operator SQL pass driven by
`memo_migrations.rollback_json`: re-insert the shell row from the
snapshot, `UPDATE messages SET conversation_id = shell_id WHERE id IN`
the snapshot's moved set, restore pins/drafts/reactions, delete the
ledger row — the ledger exists so that pass is mechanical, not because
the connector runs it.

Tests (+4 store, +1 supervisor): the fold moves deduplicated messages,
reactions, pins and merged state into the canonical row, deletes the shell
and writes the ledger
(`memo_migration_folds_the_number_shell_into_the_canonical_aci_row`);
the fold is idempotent and skips accounts without a shell or an ACI
(`memo_migration_is_idempotent_and_skips_accounts_without_shell_or_aci`);
the redirect re-keys the own-number key to the ACI and the canonical row
reads `isSelf` on both list and single-row faces
(`canonical_aci_key_redirects_the_own_number_and_marks_is_self`, beside an
extended arm in the §4.42 self-boundary test); the sync seam folds and
announces (`account_sync_backfills_the_memo_identity_and_announces_the_canonical_row`).
The integration faces ride the same keys: the note-to-self skeleton test
derives the answered ACI from the finish answer and asserts the upstream
dispatch targets it, and the phase2 account delete runs with a fold ledger
row present (the cascade face).

### 4.171 The outbound quote projection: a sent reply shows its quote pill everywhere the row is read (contract revision 1.171, 2026-10-17)

The desktop acceptance run surfaced a reply bug: a reply quoting an
earlier message reached the peer (the quote rode the upstream send), but
the local thread never rendered a quote block — not on the optimistic
seed, not at send settlement, not after a refresh or restart. The wire
contract was never the problem: §5.4 v1.7 has promised the outbound
`quote` projection since it was written. The connector simply never
produced it. An outgoing row persisted `quote_message_id` (the raw
pointer the upstream send validated at §4.6 resolve time) and nothing
else; `quote_snapshot` — the engine's normalized quote face — was
captured on inbound rows only; and the desktop's bubble renders a quote
from `view.quote` / `view.quoteSnapshot` alone. Both faces were
structurally empty on outgoing rows, so every reader of a sent reply saw
a quote-less bubble.

**The projection is derived at read time, never stored.** The stored row
gains nothing: `Store::attach_outgoing_quotes` walks a record batch the
way `attach_edits` does, groups the outgoing rows that carry a
`quote_message_id` and no projection yet by conversation, reads each
conversation's quoted target rows in one batched query, and fills
`MessageRecord.quote` in place. A row already carrying a projection is
untouched; absent stays absent; the store schema does not move. The
projection mirrors the §5.4 v1.7 face exactly: the quoted message's
Signal timestamp (`sent_at`), an author, the bounded body preview (the
target's CURRENT body, capped at the 128-codepoint §5.4 face) and the
attachment metadata (≤8 entries, contentType/filename, thumbnails absent
— the store keeps no quote thumbnails for outgoing rows).

**The author ladder is the §4.6 resolve ladder in reverse.** The author
of a quote must be an identity the desktop could itself address, or the
pill would mislead: an addressable outgoing target (status
sent/delivered/read) authors with the linked account's own number; a
direct-chat incoming target authors with the conversation peer key. A
pending own row is not yet an addressable message; a group incoming row
persists only a local sender hash; a system row has no author at all; a
retracted target (remote-deleted or admin-deleted) keeps its body bytes
in the store but its deletion face is the caller-visible truth —
projecting the stale body would resurrect retracted content in the reply
pill. Each of these degrades to an absent projection; a stored quote can
degrade, never mis-address.

**Direction discipline.** Incoming rows never join: their
`quote_snapshot` face is the engine's authoritative inbound quote and
stays exactly as persisted. The projection exists to close the one face
the store genuinely could not answer — what an own outgoing row quoted.

**The attach faces.** Read side: `messages.list`, the adjacent-media
probe, `messages.search` and the single-message face. Upstream
settlement side: the send-success answer row (the row the desktop
settles its optimistic bubble with — the pill is correct the moment the
send completes, with no extra round trip), the edit settlement, the
early-control edit flush and the live sync-mirror edit (a reply edited
from another device re-emits with its pill). The plaintext export and
audit faces stay raw — they project stored columns only, and the
projection is a read-time derivation, not stored state.

**Recorded boundaries.** A quoted target edited later re-quotes with its
current text automatically (the projection reads the live body — the
pill tracks the edit, the same semantics as the upstream quote: a
pointer, not a snapshot). A quoted target retracted later drops the pill
on the next read. Rows written before this revision project on their
first post-revision read (the pointer was always stored); nothing
backfills.

Tests (+5): the author ladder across direct-incoming / own-sent /
pending / missing targets on the list and single-row faces
(`outgoing_quote_projection_follows_the_author_ladder_and_degrades_to_absent`);
the group and retraction guards
(`group_and_retracted_targets_never_project`); the 128-codepoint preview
cap (`quote_projection_truncates_long_target_bodies_at_128_codepoints`);
the send-success and edit answer rows carrying the projection
(`complete_send_and_edit_answer_rows_carry_the_quote_projection`); the
inbound `quote_snapshot` face staying untouched
(`incoming_rows_keep_their_stored_quote_snapshot_face`).

### 4.172 retryText idempotent replay: a completed original send answers its terminal row, and the orphan sweep gets a read-only probe (contract revision 1.172, 2026-10-17)

The method probe closed the loop on a resend-refusal deadlock. The
live sequence (restart29 era, 2026-10-17): the engine's `send-done`
succeeded — the message reached the peer — but the connector service
process died before the success answer crossed the socket, so the
desktop's bubble never settled. The persisted ledger row, though, had
already recorded the truth: `sent`. When the user later tapped 重新发送,
`prepare_retry_text` saw a row that was not `failed` and refused
`RETRY_NOT_ALLOWED` — the guard that exists to prevent double-delivery
was stranding a *delivered* message with a failed bubble and no
recovery path. Message delivered, row shows failed, resend refused:
both ends clamped shut.

**The fix is replay, not a wider refusal.** Idempotent replay is the
standard semantics: the official client's persisted send job re-run
after completion answers the completed outcome (conversationJobQueue
re-queues the same job and the job layer is naturally idempotent), and
Signal iOS/Android send layers replay the recorded result on a repeated
request. The connector's first dispatch already implements exactly this
face — `prepare_send_text` answers `PreparedSend::Existing` (the
persisted row) when the clientRequestId was seen — and
`dispatch_prepared` answers that variant without touching the engine.
`prepare_retry_text` now joins the same semantics: a retry addressed at
a row whose original send already reached a terminal success state
(`sent`/`delivered`/`read`) answers the persisted terminal row
(reactions and the §4.171 outgoing-quote projection attached —
byte-shaped like the `complete_send_success` answer row), store
untouched, never re-dispatched. Replay precedes the rebuild guards: a
completed *attachment* send replays too (the replay never rebuilds, so
no bytes are lost), which is exactly what the first-send `Existing`
face does for it.

**The genuinely-not-allowed faces stay refused, with a split code.**
`unknown` answers the new `RETRY_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` — its wire outcome was
never settled, so a blind resend could double-deliver, and the host
must never auto-resend it; the dedicated code keeps that refusal
attributable apart from the rebuild guards. `RETRY_NOT_ALLOWED` now
means one thing only: a *failed* row whose rebuild the connector
refuses (the §4.134 attachment guard — the rebuild face carries
text/quote/preview, so a captioned attachment send would leave as plain
text without its bytes). `pending` keeps `RETRY_IN_FLIGHT`, a missing
row keeps `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND`, a cross-conversation address keeps
`INVALID_REQUEST`. Only the replay arm is new behavior; every refusal
that existed still exists, one of them under a more precise name.

**The orphan sweep's probe is a new read-only face, not retryText.**
The desktop's unsettled-row sweep (desktop contract 1.167) reloads a
pending/unknown bubble whose in-flight attempt died with the renderer
and must decide whether to mark it failed. Asking `messages.retryText`
to answer that question is tempting (same addressing, same ledger) and
wrong: a *failed* ledger row would be re-dispatched by it — an
automatic resend the user never asked for, the exact thing the §5 send
discipline forbids. So the connector grows `messages.getByClientRequestId`
(read lane, zero mutation, no upstream traffic): the same ledger row
addressed by the original send's idempotency key, answered with its
settled state in the messages.list row shape (reactions, edits and the
outbound quote projection attached). The sweep's decision table: the
probe answers sent/delivered/read → flip the bubble in place; pending →
leave it (the connector's outbox owns the row); failed/unknown → the
honest error arm; `MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` (the original request never
arrived) or any probe transport failure → the same honest error arm.
Wire change is additive — one method, one params shape, one error code.

**Download-guard reject attribution.** The same probe era surfaced a
live `attachments.download` INVALID_REQUEST refusal cluster that read
zero reject-detail rows: host.rs's dispatch-time probes cover the serde
shape gates, but the download face's real guards run one layer down, in
`prepare_attachment_download` / `attachment_locator_for_index`
(attachmentIndex over the inbound ceiling, attachmentIndex naming no

and shape (`target=send_latency_probe`, `stage=connector.reject-detail`)
